candidates.passage:
Parth Gohil: Congratulations to the team and the entire management for the performance. Sir, my question is 
pertaining to the Lubricant segment. Do we further foresee or anticipate any lo ss of volume in 
coming quarters or we can say that it has normalized at this level?
J. Lakshmana Rao: Yes. I think you have a very smart question. In fact, I'm also thinking it will stay there because 
we have no more public sector units to lose. And all the private sector companies value our 
relation and our quality and the consistency, which is very impo rtant. I'm not saying it's not for 
public sector, but public sector has more valuation for pricing than anything else, and it's their 
policy. And having lost all the PSU business now, we may sustain at the current levels in Lubes.
candidates.speaker: J. Lakshmana Rao
candidates.adjudication_note: Analyst framed 'no further loss/normalized'; management accepted current-level sustainability but without numeric base.

candidates.passage:
Coming back to ROCE, yes, the ROCE has leaped by about 14% from 10.2% to 12.4% and 
probably it may hit around 13.5% to 14% in the next financial year. And it was 17%, 18% 2 -3 
years ago, I agree. That was when all these greenfield projects have been starte d, investments 
have shot up in the last 3 years.
 And these investments start yielding now. This year, I would say they crossed 50% to 60% 
capacity utilization. But next year onwards, I'm confident it will be 70% plus, and they will be 
yielding to the bottom line. So probably the ROCE will start looking at around 15% by '27-'28.
candidates.speaker: J. Lakshmana Rao

candidates.passage:
Shanskar: Sir, most of my questions have been answered. Just wanted to understand on the growth 
perspective, while you have answered on volume and value terms, I just wanted to get that you 
have guided going forward on maintaining around 20% growth rate in terms of  profitability at 
EBITDA and PAT level. So are you maintaining that or is there any upside or downward 
revision?
J. Lakshmana Rao: I think we'll certainly be there. We are aiming at, at least INR210 crores EBITDA for next 
financial year, up from INR173, that's 20% price. I think we are definitely going to achieve that 
in view of not only the increasing business, but our internal improvisations and efficiency 
creation, what we are bringing through the consolidation of units. It might -- I mean, if thi ngs 
go well, I mean, nothing further damage happens through this war, we should be looking better 
than that expected EBITDA.
candidates.speaker: J. Lakshmana Rao
candidates.adjudication_note: EBITDA absolute is not part of the controlled scorable P&L metrics list, which only includes EBITDA/PBDIT margin.
